newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gold may feel pressure, test $324.00.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gold may feel pressure, test $324.00.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Gold prices may come under some pressure on Wednesday after the quiet expiry of OTC options on Tuesday, analysts said.
The market's inability to pierce resistance could lead to a test of initial support around $324.00 an ounce, they said.
GOLD
With the option expiry out of the way and speculative interest diminishing, gold chances of an upside break are fading too, analysts said.
The market's technical background was beginning to show signs of clogging up after a month in a tight range, which suggested the range could become narrower as August began.
Gold closed last night in London at $326.20/$326.70, having found confidence draining after a brief move over $328.00 attracted producer attention.
"Gold looks to have faded a little with initial support looking vulnerable to continued tests," said technical analyst Martin Squires at Rudolf Wolff and Co.
Referring to the Comex December contract, Squires noted that a close under $330.00 (Comex closed down $3.60 at $329.80) would signal tests of support at $322-$325 with a target of $318.00.

The release of U.S. economic data later this week -- new homes sales are due on Wednesday, with employment data and the NAPM data on Thursday and Friday -- would also restrain the market, dealers said.
At 0715 GMT gold was indicated at $325.90/$326.40, down 30 cents from the previous close.
SILVER
Any bullish hopes for silver were quickly abandoned on Tuesday as the market failed to generate momentum and received little support from a faltering gold price.
However, closes on the futures and spot markets suggested sideways movement would continue rather than a distinct move back towards support, analysts said.
"Technically silver is still preferred to gold," one analyst said, but added that $4.38-$4.40 needed to be more seriously tested than it had been recently if a break was to be sustained.
Silver had failed to sustain rallies over $4.40 several times, most notably when the recent high of $4.45 was struck on July 24.
With gold likely to be easing, silverr was forecast for a day in the low $4.30s.
At 0715 GMT silver was indicated at $4.34/$4.36, two cents up on the London close.
PLATINUM
Hopes earlier in the week that platinum might test recent highs had not been fulfilled, but the scope for an advance was intact unless the $420.00 support broke, analysts said.
Above the recent top of $437.00, the next step would be to $460.00
The platinum-gold spread had slipped to under $100, and $102-$103 was needed to signal a possible widening to $112.00, they said.
At 0715 GMT platinum was indicated at $424.00/$427.00, down a dollar from the London close.
--Brian Spoors London Newsroom +44 171 542 8058
